## I JUDICIAL REVIEW

## Scope and interpretation

## 54.1

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (1) This Section of this Part contains rules about judicial review. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (2) In this Section –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (a) a ‘claim for judicial review’ means a claim to review the lawfulness of –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (i) an enactment; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (ii) a decision, action or failure to act in relation to the exercise of a public function. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (b) revoked

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (c) revoked

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (d) revoked

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (e) ‘the judicial review procedure’ means the Part 8 procedure as modified by this Section;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (f) ‘interested party’ means any person (other than the claimant and defendant) who is directly affected by the claim; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (g) ‘court’ means the High Court, unless otherwise stated. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1] (Rule 8.1(6)(b) provides that a rule or practice direction may, in relation to a specified type of proceedings, disapply or modify any of the rules set out in Part 8 as they apply to those proceedings)

## Who may exercise the powers of the High Court

## 54.1A

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (1) A court officer assigned to the Administrative Court office who is –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (a) a barrister,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (b) a solicitor; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (c)a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Legal Executives or a CILEX lawyer,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] may exercise the jurisdiction of the High Court with regard to the matters set out in paragraph (2) with the consent of the President of the King’s Bench Division. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (2) The matters referred to in paragraph (1) are –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (a) any matter incidental to any proceedings in the High Court;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (b) any other matter where there is no substantial dispute between the parties; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (c) the dismissal of an appeal or application where a party has failed to comply with any order, rule or practice direction. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (3) A court officer may not decide an application for –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (a) permission to bring judicial review proceedings;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (b) an injunction;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (c) a stay of any proceedings, other than a temporary stay of any order or decision of the lower court over a period when the High Court is not sitting or cannot conveniently be convened, unless the parties seek a stay by consent. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (4) Decisions of a court officer may be made without a hearing. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (5) A party may request any decision of a court officer to be reviewed by a judge of the High Court. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (6) At the request of a party, a hearing will be held to reconsider a decision of a court officer, made without a hearing. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.1A] (7) A request under paragraph (5) or (6) must be filed within 7 days after the party is served with notice of the decision. ## When this Section must be used

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > When this Section must be used] 54.2 The judicial review procedure must be used in a claim for judicial review where the claimant is seeking –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > When this Section must be used] (a) a mandatory order;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > When this Section must be used] (b) a prohibiting order;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > When this Section must be used] (c) a quashing order; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > When this Section must be used] (d) an injunction under section 30 of the Supreme Court Act 1981 1 (restraining a person from acting in any office in which he is not entitled to act). ## When this Section may be used

## 54.3

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.3] (1) The judicial review procedure may be used in a claim for judicial review where the claimant is seeking –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.3] (a) a declaration; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.3] (b) an injunction ( GL ) . [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.3] (Section 31(2) of the Supreme Court Act 1981 sets out the circumstances in which the court may grant a declaration or injunction in a claim for judicial review)

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.3] (Where the claimant is seeking a declaration or injunction in addition to one of the remedies listed in rule 54.2, the judicial review procedure must be used)

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.3] (2) A claim for judicial review may include a claim for damages, restitution or the recovery of a sum due but may not seek such a remedy alone. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.3] (Section 31(4) of the Supreme Court Act sets out the circumstances in which the court may award damages, restitution or the recovery of a sum due on a claim for judicial review)

## Permission required

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > Permission required] 54.4 The court’s permission to proceed is required in a claim for judicial review whether started under this Section or transferred to the Administrative Court. ## Time limit for filing claim form

## 54.5

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (A1) In this rule —

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] ‘the planning acts’ has the same meaning as in section 336 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 2 ;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] ‘decision governed by the Public Contracts Regulations 2015’ means any decision the legality of which is or may be affected by a duty owed to an economic operator by virtue of regulations 89 or 90 of those Regulations (and for this purpose it does not matter that the claimant is not an economic operator); and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] ‘economic operator’ has the same meaning as in regulation 2(1) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (1) The claim form must be filed –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (a) promptly; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (b) in any event not later than 3 months after the grounds to make the claim first arose. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (2) The time limits in this rule may not be extended by agreement between the parties. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (3) This rule does not apply when any other enactment specifies a shorter time limit for making the claim for judicial review. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (4) Paragraph (1) does not apply in the cases specified in paragraphs (5), (6) and (7). [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (5) Where the application for judicial review relates to a decision made by the Secretary of State or local planning authority under the planning acts, the claim form must be filed not later than six weeks after the grounds to make the claim first arose. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (6) Where the application for judicial review relates to a decision governed by the Public Contracts Regulations 2015, the claim form must be filed within the time within which an economic operator would have been required by regulation 92(2) of those Regulations (and disregarding the rest of that regulation) to start any proceedings under those Regulations in respect of that decision. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.5] (7) Where the application for judicial review is in respect of a failure by a competent authority to comply with the Public Service Obligations in Transport Regulations 2023(1) in deciding to enter into a public services contract or make a general rule, the claim form must be filed within the applicable time period specified in regulation 24(1) of those Regulations. ## Claim form

## 54.6

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.6] (1) In addition to the matters set out in rule 8.2 (contents of the claim form) the claimant must also state –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.6] (a) the name and address of any person he considers to be an interested party;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.6] (b) that he is requesting permission to proceed with a claim for judicial review; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.6] (c) any remedy (including any interim remedy) he is claiming; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.6] (d) where appropriate, the grounds on which it is contended that the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.6] (Rules 46.24 to 46.27 make provision about costs in Aarhus Convention claims.)

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.6] (Part 25 sets out how to apply for an interim remedy)

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.6] (2) The claim form must be accompanied by the documents required by Practice Direction 54A. ## Service of claim form

## 54.7

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7] The claim form must be served on –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7] (a) the defendant; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7] (b) unless the court otherwise directs, any person the claimant considers to be an interested party,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7] within 7 days after the date of issue. ## Judicial review of decisions of the Upper Tribunal

## 54.7A

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7A] (1) Where the Upper Tribunal has refused permission to appeal against a decision of the First-tier Tribunal, no application for judicial review of the Upper Tribunal’s decision, or which relates to the First-tier Tribunal’s decision, may be made except where the question in the judicial review application is—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7A] (a) whether the application for permission to appeal was validly made to the Upper Tribunal;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7A] (b) whether the Upper Tribunal when refusing permission to appeal was properly constituted; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7A] (c) whether the Upper Tribunal is acting or has acted in bad faith or in such a procedurally defective way as amounts to a fundamental breach of the principles of natural justice. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.7A] (2) The claim form and the supporting documents must be filed no later than 16 days after the date on which notice of the Upper Tribunal’s decision was sent to the applicant. ## Acknowledgment of service

## 54.8

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (1) Any person served with the claim form who wishes to take part in the judicial review must file an acknowledgment of service in the approved form in accordance with the following provisions of this rule. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (2) Any acknowledgment of service must be –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (a) filed not more than 21 days after service of the claim form; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (b) served on –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (i) the claimant; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (ii) subject to any direction under rule 54.7(b), any other person named in the claim form,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] as soon as practicable and, in any event, not later than 7 days after it is filed. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (3) The time limits under this rule may not be extended by agreement between the parties. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (4) The acknowledgment of service –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (a) must –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (i) where the person filing it intends to contest the claim, set out a summary of his grounds for doing so; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (ii) where the person filing it intends to contest the application for permission on the basis that it is highly likely that the outcome for the claimant would not have been substantially different if the conduct complained of had not occurred, set out a summary of the grounds for doing so; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (iii) state the name and address of any person the person filing it considers to be an interested party; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (b) may include or be accompanied by an application for directions. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (5) Rule 10.3(2) does not apply. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (Section 31(3C) of the Senior Courts Act 1981(1) requires the court, where it is asked to do so by the defendant, to consider whether the outcome for the claimant would have been substantially different if the conduct complained of had not occurred.)

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] Reply to acknowledgment of service

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] 54.8A. —(1) A claimant who has been served with any acknowledgment of service in accordance with rule 54.8(2)(b)(i) may file a reply. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (2) Any reply must be—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (a)filed not more than 7 days after service of the acknowledgment of service; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (b)served on—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (i)the defendant; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (ii)any person served with the claim form,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] as soon as practicable and in any event not later than 7 days after it is filed. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (3) The time limits under this rule may not be extended by agreement between the parties. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.8] (4) Practice Direction 54A makes provision as to the content and length of any reply. ## Failure to file acknowledgment of service

## 54.9

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.9] (1) Where a person served with the claim form has failed to file an acknowledgment of service in accordance with rule 54.8, he –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.9] (a) may not take part in a hearing to decide whether permission should be given unless the court allows him to do so; but

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.9] (b) provided he complies with rule 54.14 or any other direction of the court regarding the filing and service of –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.9] (i) detailed grounds for contesting the claim or supporting it on additional grounds; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.9] (ii) any written evidence,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.9] may take part in the hearing of the judicial review. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.9] (2) Where that person takes part in the hearing of the judicial review, the court may take his failure to file an acknowledgment of service into account when deciding what order to make about costs. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.9] (3) Rule 8.4 does not apply. ## Permission given

## 54.10

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.10] (1) Where permission to proceed is given the court may also give directions. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.10] (2) Directions under paragraph (1) may include –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.10] (a) a stay ( GL ) of proceedings to which the claim relates;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.10] (b) directions requiring the proceedings to be heard by a Divisional Court. ## Service of order giving or refusing permission

## 54.11

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11] The court will serve –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11] (a) the order giving or refusing permission; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11] (ai) any certificate (if not included in the order) that permission has been granted for reasons of exceptional public interest in accordance with section 31(3F) of the Senior Courts Act 1981; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11] (b) any directions,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11] on –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11] (i) the claimant;

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11] (ii) the defendant; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11] (iii) any other person who filed an acknowledgment of service. ## Permission decision where court requires a hearing

## 54.11A

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11A] (1) This rule applies where the court wishes to hear submissions on—

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11A] (a) whether it is highly likely that the outcome for the claimant would not have been substantially different if the conduct complained of had not occurred; and if so

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11A] (b) whether there are reasons of exceptional public interest which make it nevertheless appropriate to give permission. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11A] (2) The court may direct a hearing to determine whether to give permission. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11A] (3) The claimant, defendant and any other person who has filed an acknowledgment of service must be given at least 2 days’ notice of the hearing date. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11A] (4) The court may give directions requiring the proceedings to be heard by a Divisional Court. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.11A] (5) The court must give its reasons for giving or refusing permission. ## Permission decision without a hearing

## 54.12

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (1) This rule applies where the court, without a hearing –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (a) refuses permission to proceed; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (b) gives permission to proceed –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (i) subject to conditions; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (ii) on certain grounds only. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (2) The court will serve its reasons for making the decision when it serves the order giving or refusing permission in accordance with rule 54.11. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (3) Subject to paragraph (7), the claimant may not appeal but may request the decision to be reconsidered at a hearing. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (4) A request under paragraph (3) must be filed within 7 days after service of the reasons under paragraph (2). [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (5) The claimant, defendant and any other person who has filed an acknowledgment of service will be given at least 2 days’ notice of the hearing date. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (6) The court may give directions requiring the proceedings to be heard by a Divisional Court. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.12] (7) Where the court refuses permission to proceed and records the fact that the application is totally without merit in accordance with rule 23.12, the claimant may not request that decision to be reconsidered at a hearing. ## Defendant etc. may not apply to set aside ( GL )

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > Defendant etc. may not apply to set aside ( GL )] 54.13 Neither the defendant nor any other person served with the claim form may apply to set aside ( GL ) an order giving permission to proceed. ## Response

## 54.14

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.14] (1) A defendant and any other person served with the claim form who wishes to contest the claim or support it on additional grounds must file and serve –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.14] (a) detailed grounds for contesting the claim or supporting it on additional grounds; and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.14] (b) any written evidence,

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.14] within 35 days after service of the order giving permission. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.14] (2) The following rules do not apply –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.14] (a) rule 8.5 (3) and 8.5 (4)(defendant to file and serve written evidence at the same time as acknowledgment of service); and

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.14] (b) rule 8.5 (5) and 8.5(6) (claimant to file and serve any reply within 14 days). ## Where claimant seeks to rely on additional grounds

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > Where claimant seeks to rely on additional grounds] 54.15 The court’s permission is required if a claimant seeks to rely on grounds other than those for which he has been given permission to proceed. ## Evidence

## 54.16

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.16] (1) Rule 8.6 (1) does not apply. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.16] (2) No written evidence may be relied on unless –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.16] (a) it has been served in accordance with any –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.16] (i) rule under this Section; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.16] (ii) direction of the court; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.16] (b) the court gives permission. ## Court’s powers to hear any person

## 54.17

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.17] (1) Any person may apply for permission –

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.17] (a) to file evidence; or

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.17] (b) make representations at the hearing of the judicial review. [PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.17] (2) An application under paragraph (1) should be made promptly. ## Judicial review may be decided without a hearing

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > Judicial review may be decided without a hearing] 54.18 The court may decide the claim for judicial review without a hearing where all the parties agree. ## Court’s powers in respect of quashing orders

## 54.19

[PART 54 – JUDICIAL REVIEW AND STATUTORY REVIEW > 54.19] (1) This rule applies where the court makes a quashing order in respect of the decision to which the claim relates.
